x: Good performances were put up by Alan Morrison (115th) and Fred Paget(148th) and Keith Angus a new member showed great promise in finishing 170th.

Fairclough had the race well in hand and drew away steadily with no sign of strain to win by 120yds from Cocks with a gallant Bicourt 50yds away, third. It was good to see Keith Angus getting back to form again, this 19yrs old Sheffield runner has lots of potential.

Surprise of the day was the grand form shown by Keith Angus, whose 35th place was far above expectations. The determined running of this young athlete was a joy to watch, and his rapid improvement after a long lay-off augurs well for the National when David Cocks hopes to have overcome the effects of his recent injury.

Dave Cocks started slowly, probably because he had been short of training, but he soon worked his way through to become our second scorer, a little ahead of Keith Angus who flogged his way round the two circuits with great spirit.

On Sunday 9th August a party of Belgravians plus a few extras including Jim Hogan and his wife,ex-Belgravian Keith Angus, Marianne Dew and Pat Balaam from Selsonia and Josie Newell,an import from Sheffield United,set out to make the longish trip to Langen,a small but rapidly growing town near Frankfurt.

A popular member of the Bels whilst domiciled in London in 1964 was KEITH ANGUS from Sheffield. Steadily, over the years, his performances have been improving and his latest success was a win in the Czechoslovakian Kosice Marathon classic.
